correctness.rationale: For every connected cubic graph the positive uniform equilibrium exists at all nonnegative couplings and is linearly stable exactly when I+tau A is positive definite. The Jacobian is a positive diagonal similarity of a symmetric congruence, excluding other linearly stable positive equilibria at or beyond the threshold. The exact adjacency characteristic polynomials of the Wagner graph and its one-triangle switch yield tau_c=sqrt(2)-1 and 2/(1+sqrt(17)); the latter is strictly smaller, with an exact all-common-coupling relaxation-rate gap. The standalone pure-stdlib certificate enumerates all 19,355 labeled cubic graphs at eight vertices, identifies all 19,320 connected ones by five disjoint relabeling orbits, verifies their characteristic polynomials by integer traces, and proves the sharp cutoff by comparing exact spectral root intervals. Global attraction strictly below the threshold follows from a standard strict Lyapunov identity, not finite simulation.

value.rationale: The motivated issue is the boundary between observed positive clustering–robustness correlation and a falsely inferred deterministic monotonicity law in the identical ecological model. An exact minimal connected cubic counterexample under a single degree-preserving switch establishes that triangle abundance is not sufficient to order ecological resilience even when both graphs have identical degree sequences and equilibrium abundances. The proof gives exact thresholds, an entire common-regime relaxation-rate ordering, and complete first-size classification. The eight-vertex cutoff is the smallest possible, not an arbitrary numerical slice. No claims are made about real-world empirical correlation, heterogeneous degrees or stochastic ecology.
